Results.ReviewText:
You pay for the name and the accessory world around it.
The quality of some parts is so ridiculously cheap that they should be embarrassed. The wheel caps, the screws to mount the lid handle, the plastic feet. This thing is so cost optimized that it screams cheap China product. The important parts like the grates and the kettle itself seem ok, otherwise they would get in trouble in the long run.
You also pay for its proven design, so yes, it works well, it's thought out well and you get phone customer service probably on every continent. 
But looking at the materials and build of this vs. a charcoal gravity feeder seen at your home retailer, the difference is absolutely shocking: I would guess nearly all of what you pay goes into Webers profit margin, and almost nothing into the material and build quality. For the other one with heavy cast iron grates, lot of materials, electronics, just the sheer weight, how the handles and lid feel, it's hard to believe they can make much profit for the offered price. 
It's good if a good company makes a good product for a good profit.
But this thing is probably Webers cash cow and you are the one being milked.
Results.Title: to expensive for the quality, you pay for the name

Results.ReviewText:
Pros:
I love it! It's helped me fall in love with grilling again. Everything is straight forward to use and there is no shortage of info online to get you started. My food has come out better than ever!

Cons:
The legs attach via buttons you press in and then stick the leg in place and the button pops out and locks the leg. This is nice for quick disassembly if that is what your looking for but I would prefer if the legs bolted on.

Knit picks:
The grill rolls over EXTREMELY easy when moving it while fully assembled. To move this grill you grab the handle on the front, lift up, and roll your grill where you need it to go.

The back wheels act as a pivot point so if you lift the front leg off the ground more than an inch or two it rolls forward and falls over backward. So be careful of that!

Second knit pick is the legs are just thin aluminum. This isn't the most expensive grill, and the legs are no doubt strong enough to get the job done, but this isn't a cheap grill either, and it is a major name brand. I expected a little more out of the legs build quality and attachment style.
Results.Title: *Almost* a perfect grill! 4/5

Results.ReviewText: I started with my first weber kettle back in 2007. I bought a One-gold in green. I have loved that grill to death. Thanks to some shipping issues when I got it plus moving a couple times and a whole bunch of BBQing and grilling the holes at the bottom are rusting out and it doesn't extinguish the coals like it used to. I decided to get this "premium" grill but it doesn't seem to be premium. The metal is thinner than my previous and as such either the bowl or the lid is out of round and doesn't close right. Whether that's a manufacturing tolerance issue or a shipping issue it's hard to tell (box is fine) but a thicker metal might have stayed round better. I'm concerned my reason for buying it (so that when I close the holes the fire goes out) may be hindered as a result of the lid and bowl not fitting together properly. Add to that the grill grate doesn't fit in the bowl quite right. And the last little "new normal" that doesn't work for me is that it only has one handle. I store my grill in a storage spot that has rough ground that makes rolling difficult. I would lift it in order to get it in there using both handle. Now I'm not sure how i'm going to do that. Add to that the second handle is where I hang my charcoal tongs so that's another low. All in all this will be my last Weber kettle and that's not because I think this thing is going to last. Quite to the contrary. I feel this new one won't stand up to the heavy use as well as the one I bought in 2007 did.
Results.Title: Price up, quality down

This grill features a built-in lid thermometer to monitor the temperature inside the grill, and a hinged, plated-steel cooking grate flips up on either side allowing you to easily add more fuel while cooking. Like all Weber® kettles, it’s built to last with a porcelain-enameled bowl and lid that retains heat and resist rust, peeling, and scratching, and adjustable lid and bowl dampers to fine-tune the heat for perfect results. When it’s time to clean up, the One-Touch™ cleaning system makes it neat and effortless—just swipe the lever to clear ashes into the enclosed, high-capacity ash catcher. Two wheels make it easy to roll this timeless classic to the center of the action, right where it belongs.
